title: A Universal Model for Human Mobility Prediction

problem.claim: Human mobility prediction must address both individual and collective mobility behaviors represented by trajectory and crowd-flow data.

gap.claim: Existing methods are limited to single tasks because of modal gaps between individual trajectories and crowd flows.

contributions.claim: UniMob is a universal human mobility prediction model applicable to both individual trajectory and crowd-flow prediction.
UniMob uses a multi-view mobility tokenizer and diffusion transformer to represent trajectory and flow data as spatiotemporal tokens for unified sequential modeling.
A bidirectional individual and collective alignment mechanism learns common spatiotemporal patterns and supports mutual enhancement of trajectory and flow predictions.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the bidirectional individual and collective alignment mechanism as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world datasets reportedly show that UniMob outperforms state-of-the-art baselines for trajectory and flow prediction.
In noisy and scarce data scenarios, the authors report performance improvements of more than 14% in MAPE and 25% in Accuracy@5.
The authors report that code is available online.

narrative_sequence.summary: Human mobility prediction supports urban planning, traffic control, and emergency response.
Individual trajectories and crowd flows are coupled mobility modalities, with each influencing the other.
Existing approaches remain task-specific because of the modal gap between trajectories and crowd flows.
UniMob unifies both prediction tasks using spatiotemporal tokenization, diffusion-transformer modeling, and bidirectional alignment.
The authors report superior results on real-world datasets, including improvements in noisy and scarce data settings.

source_observation.claim: Individual trajectories and crowd flows are described as mutually coupled, with aggregation operating from trajectories to flows and flow constraints affecting trajectories.

interpretation.claim: Related prediction tasks may benefit from modeling reciprocal cross-modal structure rather than treating modalities as independent.

application.claim: When designing multi-modal forecasting systems, consider shared representations and bidirectional alignment between fine-grained and aggregate data.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy transfers to mobility modalities or datasets beyond those evaluated.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, evaluation protocols, or statistical significance of the reported results.
The abstract does not describe the diffusion-transformer architecture or alignment mechanism in implementation detail.
The abstract does not establish code availability or reproducibility beyond the reported repository link.
